about: Curated third-party skills for each board seat and sub-agent archetype. Names, licences and install commands were checked against each repository on the date above. Curated is not audited: upstream changes after that date. Star counts are approximate snapshots.

obra/superpowers.summary: Engineering methodology that triggers on its own: brainstorm, plan, test-first build, sub-agent execution, review, finish.

install.note: The plugin adds the session-start bootstrap that makes the skills trigger; the skills CLI installs the skills alone. Install only from obra/superpowers: look-alike repositories exist.

mattpocock/skills.summary: Small composable engineering skills that do not try to own the process: requirement interrogation, specs, tickets, architecture.

install.note: Pick skills instead of taking the whole pack: its tdd, diagnosing-bugs and code-review overlap the process layer. Add setup-matt-pocock-skills and run /setup-matt-pocock-skills once.

DietrichGebert/ponytail.summary: Write-less-code discipline: is it needed, can it be reused, does the platform already do it. Never trades away validation, security or accessibility.

install.note: Levels: lite, full (default), ultra, off.

anthropics/claude-plugins-official.summary: Anthropic's official Claude Code plugin marketplace: first-party review and security plugins, plus vetted third-party ones.

install.note: Available in Claude Code without adding a marketplace. Skip feature-dev when another process layer is installed.

trailofbits/skills.summary: Security-audit workflows from a professional security firm.

install.note: ShareAlike licence: use it, link to it, do not copy its text into your own skills.

addyosmani/agent-skills.summary: Lifecycle engineering skills with strong shipping and operations coverage.

install.note: The full plugin is a second process layer (/spec /plan /build /review /ship); pick individual skills when superpowers is installed.

garrytan/gstack.summary: Role-based sprint commands from a YC partner: founder-style idea and plan review, real-browser QA, release engineering.

install.note: Needs Bun. It registers hooks and is a process layer of its own: call its commands by name for the jobs listed, and do not let it run the whole build alongside superpowers.

wshobson/agents.summary: Large marketplace of granular plugins; widest DevOps and infrastructure coverage, plus startup finance.

install.note: Install single plugins. Skip tdd-workflows, conductor and full-stack-orchestration when a process layer is already installed.

cloudflare/security-audit-skill.summary: Phased whole-repository security audit with a coverage ledger and independent verification.

affaan-m/ECC.summary: ECC (formerly everything-claude-code): an all-in-one harness of agents, skills, hooks and rules.

install.note: A complete process layer with its own hooks and rules. Choose ECC or superpowers as the always-on layer, not both.

EveryInc/compound-engineering-plugin.summary: Plan, work, review, and capture what was learned so each cycle makes the next one easier.

anthropics/skills.summary: Anthropic's reference skills: office documents, frontend design, web-app testing, MCP building, skill authoring.

vercel-labs/agent-skills.summary: Vercel's rule sets: interface guidelines, React performance, composition patterns.

supabase/agent-skills.summary: Supabase and Postgres best practices from the vendor.

hashicorp/agent-skills.summary: Terraform and Packer skills from the vendor.

cloudflare/skills.summary: Cloudflare platform skills from the vendor.

alirezarezvani/claude-skills.summary: Largest business-role skill library, with script-backed calculators: C-level advisors, finance, operations, product and project management.

install.note: Take the advisor and calculator skills. Leave out its board-meeting, chief-of-staff and decision-logger skills and the c-level-agents plugin: this skill already runs the board, and two protocols for the same meeting conflict. Do not install its marketing-skills next to coreyhaines31/marketingskills.

phuryn/pm-skills.summary: Product-management frameworks as skills: strategy, market research, go-to-market, execution, pricing.

anthropics/knowledge-work-plugins.summary: Anthropic's role plugins for knowledge work, with connectors: operations, finance, legal, HR, support, sales, marketing, product, design.

anthropics/financial-services.summary: Institutional-grade spreadsheet modelling: three-statement, DCF, comparables, model audit.

install.note: Built for banking and private-equity analysts; its market-data connectors are paid.

RefoundAI/lenny-skills.summary: Product and company-building judgment distilled from Lenny's Podcast and Newsletter.

install.note: Its README documents clone-and-copy; the skills CLI reads the same skills/ layout. Fall back to the manual commands if the CLI route fails.

lool-ventures/founder-skills.summary: Fundraising review written by a venture fund: deck, financial model, cap table, investment-committee simulation.

install.note: Needs Python 3.10+.

anthropics/claude-for-legal.summary: Legal practice plugins: commercial contracts, privacy, employment, product counsel.

EveryInc/charlie-cfo-skill.summary: Bootstrapped-company CFO: runway and thirteen-week cash flow.

coreyhaines31/marketingskills.summary: Broadest maintained marketing pack: positioning, copy, SEO, launch, ads, email, CRO, analytics and sales enablement around one shared product-context document.

install.note: Install the whole pack: the skills share .agents/product-marketing.md. Run product-marketing first.

blader/humanizer.summary: Removes the tells of machine-written prose and matches a voice sample.

install.note: Run it last, after editing. It improves writing; it does not claim to defeat AI detectors.

AgriciDaniel/claude-seo.summary: Deep SEO and AI-search audits: technical, schema, content briefs, clusters.

install.note: Run /seo setup after installing.

wondelai/skills.summary: Well-known business books turned into skills: positioning, messaging, offers, CRO, sales.

AgriciDaniel/claude-ads.summary: Audits of paid-ad accounts across platforms; read-only, proposes changes as drafts.

heygen-com/hyperframes.summary: Programmatic video from HTML to MP4.

remotion-dev/skills.summary: Programmatic video in React, from the Remotion team.
remotion-dev/skills.license: No licence file in the skills repository; Remotion itself has its own licence terms

pbakaus/impeccable.summary: Design vocabulary, commands and a deterministic detector for generic machine-made UI: shape, critique, audit, polish.

install.note: Run /impeccable init once. Review its settings first: its hook runs outside model approval, telemetry is on by default, and the live Apply mode can spawn an agent with permission checks bypassed.

emilkowalski/skills.summary: Motion and interaction craft from a design engineer: when and how to animate, review, performance, gestures.

jakubkrehel/skills.summary: Craft specialists: typography, colour, layout, accessibility, interface review.

nextlevelbuilder/ui-ux-pro-max-skill.summary: UI UX Pro Max: a searchable reference of styles, palettes, font pairings and UX guidelines, with a design-system generator.

install.note: Needs Python 3. Treat it as a lookup database, not as the taste layer: take palettes, pairings and rules from it, then shape the result.

Nutlope/hallmark.summary: Hallmark: themed page builds, redesigns and audits with a browser lint and hard quality gates.

install.note: A page pipeline with its own palettes and gates. Invoke it by name for a given page; do not let it and another pipeline both run on the same page.

Leonxlnx/taste-skill.summary: Taste skill: high-end marketing and showcase sites with motion, checked in a real browser.

install.note: Needs Node 22+ and Chrome. The plugin route installs a stop-hook gate; the skills CLI does not. Variants live in Leonxlnx/taste-skill-classics.

figma/mcp-server-guide.summary: Figma's official plugin and skills: design to code, code to design, libraries, Code Connect, specs.
figma/mcp-server-guide.license: Figma Developer Terms (no open-source licence file)

install.note: Needs a Figma account and the Figma MCP server.

greensock/gsap-skills.summary: Official GSAP skills: core, timelines, ScrollTrigger, React, performance.

addyosmani/web-quality-skills.summary: Measured web quality: accessibility (WCAG 2.2), Core Web Vitals, performance.

shadcn/ui.summary: Project-aware shadcn/ui knowledge from the maintainers.

Leonxlnx/imagegen-skills.summary: Brand kits and image-based design comps for agents that can generate images.

ceo.use: Strategy canvases, market sizing and competitor analysis behind the first three docket items.
CEO decision frameworks, scenario planning, competitive intelligence, board decks.
Write the PRD, review metrics, update the founder.
Pressure-test the idea before the charter and the plan before the build, the way a demanding investor would.
Get interrogated on the plan until every open branch is resolved; turn the result into a spec.
Practitioner judgment on strategy, one-way-door decisions and product-market fit.
Decks and memos for the founder or outside readers.
When raising money: deck review and a simulated investment committee.

cto.use: The process layer: how work moves from idea to merged, tested code. Exactly one process layer should be always-on.
Requirement interrogation, specs, tickets, and architecture: deep modules, a shared domain language.
Always-on restraint: build the least code that solves it. Review diffs with ponytail-review; audit debt periodically.
Independent multi-agent review of every pull request; security hooks on edits and commits.
Security review of each release's diff, defaults and dependencies.
Interface design, architecture decision records, CI/CD, observability and the launch checklist.
The all-in-one alternative to superpowers: one harness with agents, hooks, rules and stack patterns.
Real-browser QA and release engineering, called by name.
Specialised review agents (silent failures, test gaps, types) and a verified deep security scan before launch.
Browser-driven testing of web apps; building MCP servers.
Whole-repository audit with a coverage ledger. Use this or claude-security as the pre-launch audit, not both.
When the infrastructure is more than a managed platform: Kubernetes, multi-cloud, on-call.
Alternative process layer for long-lived products where capturing lessons each cycle matters most.
When the stack is React or Next.js.
When the stack uses Supabase or Postgres.
When infrastructure is managed with Terraform.

cmo.use: The marketing backbone. Run product-marketing first: it writes the shared context every other skill reads.
Last pass on anything a customer will read.
ICP, beachhead, go-to-market motion, positioning options and battlecards for docket items 2 and 7.
Campaign briefs, performance reports, and a brand voice that is discovered, written down and enforced.
Deep technical SEO and AI-search audits once there is a site. Strategy stays in marketingskills; audits happen here.
Named frameworks for positioning, messaging and offers. Feed the results into the product-marketing context.
When paid spend is live: audit the accounts.
When marketing needs video, in React. Use this or hyperframes.
When marketing needs video, from HTML.

cfo.use: Unit economics, SaaS metrics, runway and scenario maths with script-backed calculators.
Build the model as a real spreadsheet with formulas, not a table in prose.
Pricing and monetisation options for docket item 3.
A full three-statement model, valuation, and an audit of the spreadsheet before anyone relies on it.
After launch: statements, budget versus actual, month-end close, cash and invoices.
Packaging and the pricing page, with the CMO.
When raising money: model review and cap-table scenarios.
For a bootstrapped company: runway and thirteen-week cash flow.

coo.use: Process documents, runbooks, status reports, the risk register, task tracking.
Operating cadence, process mapping, capacity and vendor management.
Roadmap, OKRs, sprint plans, pre-mortems and retros.
Contract and compliance triage, hiring, and the support desk.
Practitioner judgment on goals, planning rhythm and org design.
Status updates, co-written documents, and documents for outside parties.
Once real contracts or personal data exist. Output is a draft for a qualified lawyer, never legal advice.
First drafts of the privacy policy and NDAs for lawyer review.

head-of-design.use: The primary aesthetic layer: init and shape the direction, then critique, audit and polish every surface.
Baseline for distinctive frontend work; boards and visual explorations; themes for artifacts.
Reference database for the design system: styles, palettes, font pairings, industry rules. Look things up here, then shape them.
Motion judgment: whether to animate, how, and a review of what was built.
Cheap rule audit on every user-facing change: accessibility, focus, forms, motion, typography.
New landing pages with a hard quality floor, and audits of existing ones. One pipeline per page: this or taste skill.
Showcase and marketing sites where motion carries the brand. One pipeline per page: this or hallmark.
Specialists for tuning type, colour and layout, and for reviewing interface changes.
User research and synthesis, structured critique, UX copy, and handoff specs for engineering.
The measured accessibility and performance gate before launch.
When the team works in Figma.
When motion is built with GSAP: timelines and scroll scenes done correctly.
When the product needs video: launch films, animated explainers.
When the component layer is shadcn/ui.
When the agent can generate images: brand kits and visual comps before code.

head-of-product.title: Head of Product
head-of-product.mission: Turn the board's decisions into a PRD and a backlog an engineer can build from and a tester can test from.
deliverables: `board/ceo/prd.md` kept current
User stories with acceptance criteria
A prioritised backlog with the reasoning
head-of-product.calibration: Write the PRD section and the stories for the single most important user journey. Pass if every story can be tested without asking a question.

stack.use: Writing the PRD, stories and priorities
Specifying a feature; updating the roadmap after a decision
Resolving open questions before writing; cutting a spec into tickets

market-analyst.title: Market Analyst
market-analyst.mission: Keep the board's picture of the market and the competition true and sourced.
deliverables: Competitor profiles
Market-size estimates with their assumptions
A short alert when a competitor moves
market-analyst.calibration: Profile the closest competitor on one page. Pass if every claim carries a source or is labelled as an assumption.

stack.use: Profiling competitors, sizing the market
Tracking competitor moves over time
Writing the brief the board reads

tech-lead.title: Tech Lead
tech-lead.mission: Build the plan cycle by cycle: tested, reviewed, working code for each story.
deliverables: Merged, tested code for the cycle's stories
A demo of each story against its acceptance criteria
Notes on anything that changed the plan
tech-lead.calibration: Implement the smallest story end to end, tests first. Pass if the CTO would merge the diff unchanged.

stack.use: Every task: test first, verify before claiming done, request review
Always on: the least code that solves it
Cutting work into tickets; shaping modules

qa-lead.title: QA Lead
qa-lead.mission: Try to break every story before it is called done, as someone who did not write it.
deliverables: A test plan per story
Defect reports with reproduction steps
A go / no-go line for each release
qa-lead.calibration: Write and run a test plan for one finished story. Pass if it finds a real defect or shows convincingly that there is none.

stack.use: Driving the app in a real browser
Full browser QA pass before a release
Finding test gaps and silent failures in a diff
Evidence before any claim that something works

security-lead.title: Security Lead
security-lead.mission: Find the ways this product can be attacked or can leak data before someone else does.
deliverables: A threat model
A security review of each release
Findings ranked by exploitability, with fixes
security-lead.calibration: Review the authentication flow. Pass if findings are ranked by how exploitable they are and each has a concrete fix.

stack.use: Reviewing each release's diff, defaults and dependencies
Continuous guardrails; a deep scan before launch
Hardening checklist during the build

devops-lead.title: DevOps Lead
devops-lead.mission: Make shipping boring: CI, environments, observability, and a rollback that has been tried.
deliverables: A CI pipeline that runs the tests on every change
Reproducible environments
Monitoring, alerts and a tested rollback
devops-lead.calibration: Set up CI on every push and a one-command rollback. Pass if both are demonstrated, not described.

stack.use: Pipelines, instrumentation, the launch checklist
Deployment strategy and monitoring on larger infrastructure
Release and canary checks

head-of-sales.title: Head of Sales
head-of-sales.mission: Turn the positioning into a pipeline: find the right accounts, start conversations, and learn why deals are won or lost.
deliverables: A target-account list with the reason for each
Outreach sequences and call preparation
Battlecards and objection handling
A weekly pipeline review
head-of-sales.calibration: Build a list of ten target accounts with a one-line reason each and draft the first message to one of them. Nothing is sent. Pass if the CMO would send that message.

stack.use: The daily sales loop, from research to pipeline review
Outbound sequences and sales collateral, in the product-marketing context
Battlecards; checking an account against the ICP
Outbound method and negotiation
Before any message leaves your folder

head-of-growth.title: Head of Growth
head-of-growth.mission: Find what moves acquisition and activation, by running small measured experiments.
deliverables: A funnel audit
An experiment backlog ranked by expected impact and cost
A readout of each experiment
head-of-growth.calibration: Audit the signup funnel and propose three experiments. Pass if each names its metric, its expected effect, and what it costs to run.

stack.use: Funnel audits, experiments and measurement
Structuring an experiment
The readout the CMO takes to the board

head-of-content.title: Head of Content
head-of-content.mission: Earn attention with content people search for and want to read, in the brand's voice.
deliverables: A content plan tied to search demand
Finished articles and social posts
An SEO audit after each release of the site
head-of-content.calibration: Produce the first month's content plan and one finished article. Pass if the article reads as written by a person who knows the customer.

stack.use: Planning, writing and optimising content
Content briefs, topic clusters, technical and AI-search audits
Last pass on every piece

financial-analyst.title: Financial Analyst
financial-analyst.mission: Build and maintain the financial model, and report actuals against it.
deliverables: `board/cfo/model.xlsx` with an assumptions sheet
Three scenarios
A monthly budget-versus-actual note
financial-analyst.calibration: Build the twelve-month model from the charter's assumptions with three scenarios. Pass if every output traces to an assumption cell and the model survives an audit.

stack.use: Every model is a real spreadsheet with formulas
Building the model; auditing it before the CFO sees it
Ratios, SaaS metrics and their benchmarks
Startup-shaped projections

pricing-lead.title: Pricing Lead
pricing-lead.mission: Find the price and packaging that customers accept and the model needs.
deliverables: Pricing options with the reasoning for each
A pricing-page brief for the CMO and Head of Design
A plan to test the price
pricing-lead.calibration: Propose three pricing structures. Pass if each states the customer it favours, the metric it optimises, and its effect on the model.

stack.use: Generating and comparing pricing options
Packaging and the pricing page
Price tests and their revenue effect

controller.title: Controller
controller.mission: Keep the books true once money moves: cash, invoices, reconciliation, month-end.
deliverables: A monthly cash-flow snapshot
Reconciled accounts
A list of overdue invoices and what was done about each
controller.calibration: Produce this month's cash-flow snapshot and list every unreconciled item. Pass if the CFO can tie it to the bank balance.

stack.use: The monthly close and the cash position
Workpapers

head-of-project.title: Head of Project
head-of-project.mission: Keep the plan true: who does what by when, what depends on what, and which date is at risk first.
deliverables: A milestone roadmap with owners and dependencies
`board/STATUS.md` kept current
A weekly status report and a risk register
head-of-project.calibration: Turn the approved plan into a milestone roadmap with owners, dependencies and the critical path. Pass if it names the first date at risk and why.

stack.use: Roadmap, sprint plans, pre-mortems and retros
Cutting work into tickets, triaging incoming work, handing off between sessions
Status reports, the risk register, task tracking
Portfolio and sprint health checks

legal-counsel.title: Legal and Compliance Lead
legal-counsel.mission: Spot legal and compliance exposure early and prepare drafts for a qualified lawyer to review. Never the final word on a legal question.
deliverables: A list of the legal documents the product needs before launch
First drafts for lawyer review
A compliance checklist with open items
legal-counsel.calibration: List the legal documents this product needs before launch and outline the privacy policy. Pass if each item says why it applies to this product.

stack.use: Triage of contracts and compliance questions
Vendor agreements, data-processing agreements, privacy impact assessments
First drafts

head-of-customer-success.title: Head of Customer Success
head-of-customer-success.mission: Make sure customers get an answer and get value, and bring what they say back to the board.
deliverables: A help centre
Reply drafts for incoming tickets
A monthly summary of what customers ask for and complain about
head-of-customer-success.calibration: Write one help-centre article and draft replies to three realistic tickets. Pass if the COO would send them as written.

stack.use: The support loop
Health scores and churn risk
Before any reply goes to a customer

ux-researcher.title: UX Researcher
ux-researcher.mission: Replace the board's assumptions about users with evidence.
deliverables: Interview guides and usability test plans
Syntheses of what users said, as themes with quotes
A list of assumptions that the evidence contradicts
ux-researcher.calibration: Write an interview guide for the target user and synthesise three existing sources of feedback into themes. Pass if no question in the guide leads the witness.

stack.use: Planning research and synthesising it
Interview scripts; mapping findings to opportunities
Asking questions people cannot answer politely

design-system-lead.title: Design System Lead
design-system-lead.mission: Build and guard the design system: tokens and components that make every screen consistent by default.
deliverables: `board/design/design-system.md` and the tokens in code
Core components with all their states
An audit of each new screen against the system
design-system-lead.calibration: Build the tokens and three core components. Pass if they clear the audit with no blocking finding.

stack.use: Documenting the system; auditing and polishing components
Looking up palettes, pairings and rules when defining tokens
Tuning the type scale, the colour system and spacing
Auditing for hard-coded values; handoff specs

motion-designer.title: Motion Designer
motion-designer.mission: Give the product motion that explains and delights without slowing anyone down.
deliverables: Motion principles for the product
The key interactions, animated
A motion review of each release
motion-designer.calibration: Animate the product's key interaction. Pass if it holds 60 fps on a mid-range phone and respects reduced-motion.

stack.use: Deciding what to animate, building it, reviewing it
Timelines and scroll scenes when GSAP is the library
Video: launch films and explainers
